scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Scalar Potentials and Slow Clocks for Forced Fluid Computation” (preprints/Scalar-Potentials-and-Slow-Clocks-for-Forced-Fluid-Computation-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 82005335f0aac60f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a positive computable viscosity ν. A deterministic one-tape machine and finite input effectively determine a smooth force on [0, ∞) × R3, supported in one compact spatial set for all time, whose solution from zero velocity has pressure zero and satisfies ∥∂j t Dα x u(t)∥∞ + ∥∂j t Dα x f(t)∥∞ ≤ Cj,α(1 + t)−1−j for every j ≥ 0 and spatial multi-index α. The particle initially at the origin enters {x1 < −1} exactly when the machine halts. Every displayed derivative belongs to space-time L2, and the kinetic energy is uniformly bounded. Uniqueness holds among smooth classical solutions with, for every finite T, u ∈ C([0, T]; H2 ) ∩ C1 ([0, T]; L2 ), p ∈ C([0, T]; H1 ), sup [0,T]×R3 (|u| + |∇u|) < ∞. The formulas remain valid for any fixed positive real viscosity, with evaluation relative to that parameter.
